Solution 1 is wrong because it places square $ACMN$ on the same side of $AC$ as $B$, so it is not external. Solutions 2 and 3 are wrong because their final values do not match the correct area.

**Coordinates.** Take $B=(0,0)$, $C=(50,0)$, $A=(-39.6,67.2)$. This gives $AB=78$, $AC=112$, $BC=50$, and $[ABC]=1680$. The triangle is counterclockwise.

**Outward squares.** For a counterclockwise edge $P\to Q$, the outward offset is $R(Q-P)$ with $R(x,y)=(y,-x)$.

- Square on $AB$: offset $(-67.2,-39.6)$, so $X=(-67.2,-39.6)$, $Y=(-106.8,27.6)$.
- Square on $BC$: offset $(0,-50)$, so $P=(50,-50)$, $Q=(0,-50)$.
- Square on $CA$: offset $(67.2,89.6)$, so $M=(117.2,89.6)$, $N=(27.6,156.8)$.

Solution 1 used $M=(-17.2,-89.6)$, which lies on $B$'s side of $AC$, so its square is not external.

**Midpoints.**
- $L_1=\tfrac{M+P}{2}=(83.6,\,19.8)$
- $L_2=\tfrac{Q+X}{2}=(-33.6,\,-44.8)$
- $L_3=\tfrac{N+Y}{2}=(-39.6,\,92.2)$

**Area.** With $L_2-L_1=(-117.2,-64.6)$ and $L_3-L_1=(-123.2,72.4)$, the cross product is $(-117.2)(72.4)-(-64.6)(-123.2)=-16444$. So the area is $\tfrac12\cdot 16444 = 8222$.

I also checked the midpoint formulas symbolically: $L_2-L_1=(B-C)+\tfrac12R(B+C-2A)$ and $L_3-L_2=(A-B)+\tfrac12R(A+B-2C)$, which reproduce the same vectors.

The correct area is $8222$, not $270$, $2250$, or $1260$.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
